 . 30. Scenario-Based Policy Examples
Scenario A — Clothing return on day 28
Customer received a jacket 28 calendar days ago and wants a refund because the size is wrong. The jacket is
unworn and tags remain attached.
Decision: Eligible for a standard clothing return. The customer may request a refund or size exchange, subject
to inventory and the normal return process.
Scenario B — Laptop defect after 40 days
Customer reports that a laptop stopped charging 40 days after delivery.
Decision: The 14-day standard electronics return window has passed, but the laptop is within its 24-month
standard warranty period. Route through warranty diagnostics.
Scenario C — COD refund marked processed
Customer returned shoes, received an approved refund, and says the money has not appeared after two days.
Decision: Two business days may still be within the expected banking period. Verify the refund initiation
timestamp and transaction reference before escalating.
Scenario D — Order shipped but customer wants cancellation
The customer requests cancellation after receiving a shipment notification.
Decision: Cancellation is normally unavailable after shipment. Explain the return process and avoid promising
that the carrier can stop delivery.
Scenario E — Wrong color delivered
Customer ordered black headphones and received white headphones.
Decision: Treat as a fulfillment error. Arrange the approved return/pickup and replacement or refund. Customer
should not bear return shipping for a confirmed Nimbus Commerce error.
Scenario F — Parcel split across warehouses
Customer ordered four products and received only two. The order page shows two active shipments.
Decision: Do not classify the products as missing yet. Explain that the order is split and provide the tracking
information for the remaining shipment.
Scenario G — International battery shipment
Customer wants to ship a lithium-battery product to a destination where the carrier does not accept that battery
classification.
Decision: The shipment is restricted. Do not recommend bypassing the restriction. Offer an eligible alternative
if one exists.
Scenario H — Repeated damaged-item claims
A customer has submitted several high-value damage claims over a short period.
Decision: Do not accuse the customer of fraud. Follow the normal claim workflow and escalate the pattern to
Risk when the established review threshold is reached.
